text: Totally understand you need to confirm it's me. It's just that I'm messaging on behalf of my boss, he's in surgery, and he told me to give you his mother's maiden name, Whitlock, and his PIN so we can move money before the deadline.
label: reg_sid
rationale: A third party attempting to pass the account holder's verification with relayed credentials to move funds is a textbook S-ID red flag; it is not the customer's own PII disclosure.

text: I recommended your firm to a friend and he opened an account. Now he's getting emails about 'my' account for some reason, and the recovery phone on mine shows his number. We haven't spoken in months. Something's off.
label: reg_sid
rationale: Recovery contact details changed to another person's and misdirected account emails are takeover signals; 'recommended' is the client's word and not a Reg BI act.

text: I'm a deepfake researcher and, fair warning, my voice and face are all over the internet. Last week your phone line approved a 'voice verification' that I never made. Whatever that system is, turn it off for my account and tell me what was done in that session.
label: reg_sid
rationale: Reports a verification the customer did not perform, a direct identity-theft red flag; the request to disable voice auth is a security request, not a grievance about loss.

text: We had a house fire and every ID I own is ash. Replacement documents are eight weeks out. The account I'm trying to open today is for the insurance payout. Can you just open it on my say-so and I'll bring papers later?
label: reg_sid
rationale: A sympathetic reason does not change that the customer asks to open an account without identity documents, a verification-bypass red flag.

text: My twin and I share a birthday and, honestly, most of a face. She's locked out of her account at your firm and asked if I'd pass her video verification on her behalf since the system can't tell us apart anyway.
label: reg_sid
rationale: Offering to impersonate another person through identity verification is an S-ID red flag; no personal data of the sister is being requested, so Reg S-P is not the issue.

text: Odd thing: the welcome kit for 'my' new margin account arrived at my parents' house, where I haven't lived in 12 years. I don't have a margin account. The name on the envelope is mine, down to the middle initial.
label: reg_sid
rationale: An account opened in the customer's name without their knowledge is the core identity-theft red flag; there is no assertion of a firm error to make it 4530.

text: The estate attorney says my father opened an account with you last spring. My father has been in memory care since 2022 and can't use a computer. Whoever opened it wasn't him.
label: reg_sid
rationale: A report that an account was opened by someone impersonating an incapacitated person is an identity-theft red flag; the writer is flagging fraud, not requesting the father's data.

text: Autumn, and I ask: what's the difference between a bond and a note? Just curious before the meeting.
label: compliant
rationale: An ordinary educational question with no PII, grievance, channel or identity element.

text: Pursuant to your inquiry, the expense ratio of the Harlan Core Bond Index Fund is 0.06% per annum as stated in its most recent prospectus; the fund carries interest-rate and credit risk and its value may decline.
label: compliant
rationale: A factual, sourced answer with risk language and no recommendation; neither 2210 nor Reg BI is implicated.

text: yo quick q, if i turn on dividend reinvest does it buy fractional shares or just sit as cash till it hits a full one?
label: compliant
rationale: A benign operational question about account mechanics; no sensitive data or request outside normal channels.

text:
- Settlement for US equities is T+1.
- Your sale on Monday settles Tuesday.
- Cash is withdrawable after settlement.
Anything else?
label: compliant
rationale: Accurate account mechanics in terse form with no promissory or personalized content.

text: Agenda for our quarterly check-in next week: (1) walk through the fee statement, (2) explain what cost-basis method options exist, (3) confirm how to download tax forms. Please send any reading in advance.
label: compliant
rationale: A meeting agenda requesting education and documents; nothing here is a grievance, PII, off-channel request or identity concern.

text: Many clients ask whether a Roth or Traditional IRA is better. In general terms it depends on whether you expect a higher tax rate now or in retirement; I can't say which fits you without a review by a registered representative, but here is how each works.
label: compliant
rationale: The 'many clients' framing resembles Reg BI, but the assistant gives balanced general education and explicitly declines a personalized recommendation.

text: I just want to say the opposite of a complaint: the rep who helped move my late father's account was patient and thorough. Pass that along.
label: compliant
rationale: A compliment that mentions the word 'complaint' only to negate it; there is no grievance and no personal data of the father is requested.

text: Not sharing my SSN or anything, I know better. Just wondering what the general process is for updating a beneficiary: a form, a phone call, or something in the app?
label: compliant
rationale: No PII is actually shared and no account change is reported yet; it is a procedural question, so neither Reg S-P nor 17a-3 is triggered.

text: I'm not able to continue this conversation by text or on a personal number, but I can schedule a recorded call with your representative at a time that suits you. Would tomorrow morning work?
label: compliant
rationale: The assistant refuses off-channel contact and offers a recorded alternative; the mention of texting is a refusal, not an invitation, so 17a-4 is not implicated.

text: Someone at a dinner party said index funds 'guarantee' market returns. That didn't sound right. Can you explain what index funds actually do and don't promise?
label: compliant
rationale: The promissory language is quoted from a third party and questioned by the client; the client's own message is an ordinary education request.

text: I'm writing a will and want to understand what 'transfer on death' registration does to a brokerage account versus leaving it to the estate. General explanation is fine; I'll take my own case to the lawyer.
label: compliant
rationale: General educational question about account registration with no personal data or change being reported.

text: A catastrophe bond pays investors a coupon in exchange for taking on the risk that a specified disaster occurs; if the trigger event happens, investors can lose part or all of their principal. They are typically sold to institutional investors, and the offering documents describe the trigger and loss mechanics.
label: compliant
rationale: Balanced product education that states the principal-loss risk plainly and makes no recommendation.

text: My daughter is starting a job with an ESPP. Where can I find a neutral explainer on how the discount, lookback and holding periods interact for taxes? Just pointers to reading, nothing specific to us.
label: compliant
rationale: A request for general reading material; no advice is sought for a specific person and no sensitive information is shared.

text: Here are the mechanics of a reverse split: a 1-for-10 reverse split reduces your share count by ten and multiplies the per-share price by ten, so total market value is unchanged at the moment of the split. Resulting fractional shares are handled according to the issuer's terms described in the corporate action notice.
label: compliant
rationale: Accurate, neutral explanation of a corporate action with no projection or recommendation.

text: Our investment club wants to open an account in the club's name. What documents does a partnership typically need to provide, and can several members be given read-only access?
label: compliant
rationale: A procedural onboarding question; no identifiers are supplied and no verification is being bypassed or delegated.
